subject: sentences
title: Moon and farm sentences
about: Fifteen sentences adding CKLA Unit 3 (oo as in moon and look, ou, oi, aw) and Unit 4 (er, ar, or, two-syllable words, past-tense -ed) plus their tricky words, including days of the week and today, yesterday, tomorrow. Expected December to January.
tip: For a two-syllable word like sister or butter, have him cover the second half, read the first half, then read the whole word.

cards.text: Look at the big round moon.
cards.note: oo in look is the short oo, oo in moon is the long oo; ou in round says /ou/

cards.text: We cook food in a pot.
cards.note: cook has the short oo, food has the long oo

cards.text: The farm dog ran down the hill.
cards.note: ar says /ar/ in farm; down is a tricky word

cards.text: I saw a shark at the zoo.
cards.note: aw says /aw/ in saw; ar says /ar/ in shark; oo in zoo is the long oo

cards.text: Mark has a fork and a spoon.
cards.note: Mark is a name, capital M; or says /or/ in fork; oo in spoon is the long oo

cards.text: Her sister has a red car.
cards.note: er says /er/ in her; sister has two parts: sis + ter; ar says /ar/ in car

cards.text: Should we jump in the pool?
cards.note: should: ould says ood; oo in pool is the long oo

cards.text: Dad found a coin in the sand.
cards.note: ou in found says /ou/ as in ouch; oi in coin says /oi/

cards.text: The cat jumped on the porch.
cards.note: jumped: ed says /t/; or says /or/ in porch
or says /or/ in corn; Monday: a day of the week, capital M
today is a tricky word; or says /or/ in storm; ou in loud says /ou/
tomorrow is a tricky word; cook has the short oo

cards.text: The kids yawned because it was late.
cards.note: yawned: ed says /d/; because: starts like bee, ends like cause
yesterday is a tricky word; ducks ends with ck and s
could: ould says ood; butter has two parts: but + ter
